item.title: Fonds Podiumkunsten: Foreign Performances or Concerts in the Netherlands (round 4, 2026)
item.description:
Organisation: Fonds Podiumkunsten (Performing Arts Fund NL)

Location: Activity must take place in the Netherlands. Applicants from Aruba, Bonaire, Curacao, Sint Maarten, Saba and Sint Eustatius are also in scope. No city or region restriction.

Award: Maximum EUR 25,000 per production, capped at EUR 75,000 for an applicant presenting multiple productions. Calculated on travel and transport costs of the foreign artists and their production only. EUR 267,500 available per round shared across this scheme and two sibling internationalisation schemes. Fees, venue and production costs stay with the applicant. No application fee.

Duration: Single performances or a short run of concerts within one programme or festival edition.

Deadline: 23 Sep 2026

Fonds Podiumkunsten's route for Dutch festivals and venues bringing in exceptional foreign performing arts and concerts that Dutch audiences would otherwise not see. The applicant must be a Netherlands-registered legal entity running a venue or festival and carrying artistic and financial responsibility for its own programme, so individuals and sole traders cannot apply. Grants are calculated from travel and transport costs of the incoming artists, at a maximum of EUR 25,000 per production and EUR 75,000 per applicant across several productions. The core test is that the foreign work is rarely or never seen in the Netherlands and substantially enriches the existing Dutch offer, which favours experimental, non-canonical and cross-disciplinary programming over mainstream touring. Experimental music and sound-art programming is not excluded; the selection criterion is rarity and added value, not genre. Applications go through the Mijn Fonds portal and there is no fee. Four rounds run each year. TIMING: because the scheme competes against a shared EUR 267,500 per-round pot and assessment takes several weeks after the deadline, organisers should apply at least one full round ahead of the performance date and must not have the activity already underway. Success rate in 2025 was 60 percent of 33 applications.

item.title: Gemeente Utrecht: Project Subsidy Culture (Projectsubsidie Cultuur, round 3 2026)
item.description:
Organisation: Gemeente Utrecht (Municipality of Utrecht)

Location: Activity must have a presentation moment in Utrecht and benefit residents of the municipality of Utrecht. City-restricted by presentation location, not by applicant residence.

Award: Category A: EUR 1,000 to 5,000. Category B: EUR 5,000 to 20,000. No fixed co-financing percentage, but a budget and coverage plan is mandatory. eHerkenning purchase costs may be included in the budget and are reimbursed if awarded. No application fee.

Duration: Single project.

Deadline: 25 Sep 2026

Utrecht's main project fund for cultural activity with a public presentation in the city, covering all art forms including experimental and cross-disciplinary work. Individuals, foundations, associations and companies are all eligible. Two bands apply: Category A of EUR 1,000 to 5,000 assessed on artistic importance and entrepreneurship, and Category B of EUR 5,000 to 20,000 which adds meaning for the city as a third criterion. The activity must be exceptional or innovative, or otherwise of value to the city, its residents or the Utrecht cultural sector; professional projects and amateur, education or participation projects both qualify. Three rounds run each year and the next closes 25 September 2026 at 17:00 CET. TIMING RULE, which catches applicants out: for professional arts applications the presentation may not take place earlier than 13 weeks after the round's closing date, and for participatory applications the project may not start earlier than 13 weeks after that date, so a 25 September 2026 application supports activity from late December 2026 onward. Decisions are issued no later than 13 weeks after the closing date, following review by an independent Adviescommissie Projectsubsidies. Documentation is capped at 15 pages, or 5 pages if a video is included. Applications go through mijnsubsidie.utrecht.nl with DigiD or eHerkenning. Utrecht also runs a rolling Impulssubsidie Cultuur of up to EUR 2,500 for first-time applicants only, open through 31 December 2026.

item.title: BNG Cultuurfonds: Project Grants (round closing September 2026)
item.description:
Organisation: Stichting BNG Cultuurfonds (BNG Bank)

Location: Project must take place in Dutch municipalities; projects largely abroad are excluded. Not region-restricted, but 2026 priority goes to Limburg, Overijssel, Drenthe and Zeeland.

Award: EUR 5,000 minimum to EUR 15,000 maximum. The request must represent 5 to 35 percent of total project funding, so at least 65 percent co-financing is required. The fund is never the sole financier, and place-specific projects require at least one local or regional co-financier. No application fee.

Duration: Single project with a clear start and end; must be executed within two years of award. A grantee cannot reapply for 36 months.

Deadline: 27 Sep 2026

BNG Cultuurfonds funds arts and culture projects that add value for Dutch municipalities and their inhabitants, explicitly including temporary exhibitions, public programmes and festivals developed by professional makers. Media art, digital culture and cross-disciplinary work qualify as long as a professional maker's artistic vision leads the project. Only stichtingen (foundations) may apply: no sole traders, associations, individuals, or foundations in formation. Applications go by email to aanvraag.cultuurfonds@bngbank.nl with a signed form, a project plan of at most 3,500 words, a specified budget and coverage plan, current statutes and a recent KvK extract. The grant is EUR 5,000 to 15,000 and can cover no more than 35 percent of the budget. TIMING IS THE MAIN TRAP: for the 27 September 2026 deadline, feedback comes at the end of December 2026 and the project may not start before 1 January 2027, with applications for earlier-starting projects rejected outright with no exceptions. Missing documents are flagged up to one week before the deadline, so anything submitted in the final week cannot be corrected. Plan for roughly four months of lead time. Excluded: amateur art, talent development, education-focused projects, semi-permanent public art, publications, building or renovation, and regular operating costs. Further rounds: 3 January 2027, 28 March 2027, 27 June 2027, 3 October 2027 and 2 January 2028.

item.title: Stichting Cultuur Eindhoven: Project Subsidy (Projecten, 2027 round 1)
item.description:
Organisation: Stichting Cultuur Eindhoven

Location: Eindhoven. The applicant must be a legal entity based in Eindhoven and the activity must serve the Eindhoven cultural offering. City-restricted at the applicant level.

Award: Maximum EUR 35,000 per application and maximum 80 percent of eligible costs, so at least 20 percent co-financing is required. No application fee.

Duration: Single project within the 2025-2028 policy period.

Deadline: 30 Sep 2026

The mid-size project strand of Stichting Cultuur Eindhoven, the arm's-length body that distributes the city's culture budget, and the main municipal route for an Eindhoven organisation to fund a festival, exhibition or public programme. Awards go up to EUR 35,000 and cover a maximum of 80 percent of eligible costs, so at least a fifth of the budget must come from elsewhere. Unlike the Snelgeld strand this route is closed to individuals: only private-law legal entities established in Eindhoven may apply. Rounds run three times a year in fixed windows; the next opens 1 September and closes at 17:00 on 30 September 2026, which is round 1 of the 2027 cycle. TIMING: the decision lag is long by municipal standards at up to 13 weeks after the submission window closes, so a September 2026 application is decided around the end of December 2026 and activity should be planned for 2027. Given Eindhoven's design and technology profile, media-art, design and creative-technology programming fits the remit particularly well. The parallel Snelgeld strand offers up to EUR 5,000 on rolling intake, reopening 1 September 2026 and running until 31 December 2026 or until the tranche budget is exhausted, whichever comes first.

item.title: Mondriaan Fund: Inside-Out Art Museum Residency 2027 (Beijing)
item.description:
Organisation: Mondriaan Fund / Inside-Out Art Museum

Location: Beijing, China. For visual artists, curators and critics based in the Netherlands or the Caribbean part of the Kingdom, funded by the Mondriaan Fund.

Award: Subsidy of EUR 8,478 for an artist or EUR 5,622 for a curator/critic toward travel, material and living costs (a 10 percent personal contribution is automatically deducted by the Mondriaan Fund); studio, living space and Inside-Out Art Museum support are paid directly by the Mondriaan Fund. For a selected duo the total is increased proportionally to cover the second applicant's travel and accommodation. Contribution for Caribbean-based residents can be increased for higher travel costs. No application fee.

Duration: Three months: 1 March to 30 May 2027 (flexible start date, set by IOAM in consultation with the resident)

Deadline: 27 Aug 2026

Mondriaan Fund-supported working period at Inside-Out Art Museum (IOAM) in Beijing, one of China's leading independent platforms for contemporary art and research. The museum combines exhibitions, critical inquiry and public programmes, giving residents room for in-depth research, experimentation and exchange within a Chinese art scene that is otherwise hard to access from Europe. The residency is framed as cultural exchange rather than production to deadline: IOAM works with a flexible model that takes the resident's other obligations into account and sets the exact start date in consultation with the selected candidate. WHO: visual artists, curators and critics based in the Netherlands or the Caribbean part of the Kingdom. Duos and collaborations may apply (two artists, two curators/critics, or a combination who structurally make work together, submitting a joint plan for the work period that leads to a single result, and who live and work together in the same space during the residency), but each individual must submit a separate application; the apartment is well suited to duos or partnerships. WORK PERIOD: one period of three months, 1 March to 30 May 2027, with room for one artist or duo; you can state a preference for the work period in the application form. Selection is by advisory committee; read the Mondriaan Fund Residency explanation for the conditions, assessment and checklist, plus the fund's general terms and conditions, before applying. DEADLINE: Thursday 27 August 2026, before 16:00 Dutch time / 10:00 Caribbean time.

item.title: Gemeente Rotterdam: Project Subsidy Culture (Projectsubsidie Cultuur, September 2026 round)
item.description:
Organisation: Gemeente Rotterdam (Municipality of Rotterdam)

Location: Activity must serve a Rotterdam interest and take place in or for Rotterdam. City-restricted by relevance of the activity rather than by applicant address.

Award: No stated per-application cap. Annual pot EUR 1,632,000 split into six rounds of EUR 272,000, with roughly 130 applications per round. Discipline sub-caps: book writing max EUR 4,500; moving image R&D max EUR 4,000; moving-image production max EUR 12,500; post-production max EUR 4,000. Applicants must demonstrably seek other funds or sponsors. Awards over EUR 50,000 require an auditor's statement at reporting, at the applicant's cost. No application fee.

Duration: Single one-off project.

Deadline: 01 Sep 2026

Rotterdam's standing project fund for one-off artistic and cultural activity, and the most accessible municipal route for festivals, exhibitions and public programmes in the city. The discipline list names e-culture outright alongside moving image and artistic film, design and fashion, visual arts and photography, architecture, spoken word and all hybrid forms, so media-art and creative-technology programming is squarely in scope. Both non-profit legal entities and natural persons may apply, so individual artists are eligible. There is no published maximum per application; the real constraint is the EUR 272,000 available per round against roughly 130 competing applications. Six rounds run every year with fixed closing dates on the first of January, March, May, July, September and November. TIMING RULE: the activity may not start until eight weeks after the closing date of the round applied in, so a 1 September 2026 application supports activity from late October 2026 onward. Decisions normally arrive within eight weeks of the round deadline, extendable to 20 weeks. Associations and foundations apply via eHerkenning, individuals via DigiD. Organisations already receiving Rotterdamse Culturele Basis, Cultuurplan, Impulsregeling, national BIS, Lokale Culturele Programmering or a CBK Rotterdam practice contribution are excluded.

item.title: Kunstraad Groningen: Two-Year Programme Scheme (Tweejarige Programmaregeling, 2027-2028)
item.description:
Organisation: Kunstraad Groningen, on behalf of the municipality and province of Groningen

Location: Municipality and province of Groningen. The applicant organisation must be based and active in Groningen. Region-restricted.

Award: EUR 5,000 minimum to EUR 40,000 maximum per year across two years, so up to EUR 80,000 total. Covers a maximum of one third of total project costs, requiring roughly 67 percent co-financing. Annual scheme budget EUR 325,000. No application fee.

Duration: Two years of programming, covering 2027 and 2028.

Deadline: 01 Sep 2026

This is the Groningen scheme that actually funds festivals, and the correct counterpart to the Kunstraad's Projectenregeling, which explicitly excludes festivals and recurring programmes and redirects them here. It supports coherent, continuous public activity across 2027 and 2028 in all arts and heritage disciplines, naming recurring production series, festivals and programme lines as eligible, with no exclusion of media art, digital culture or experimental sound work. Annually recurring festivals with a year-round paid organisation are explicitly named as eligible applicants. Awards run from EUR 5,000 to 40,000 per year against an annual pot of EUR 325,000, capped at one third of total project costs, so two thirds must come from municipal funds, national funds, box office or own contribution. Unusually, the money may also be used to strengthen the organisation itself on the business side, not only to pay for programme content. The application window is 1 July to 1 September 2026, closing at 23:59, and only applications received on time are processed. Applications must be submitted in Dutch via the Mijn Kunstraad portal with fair-pay standards applied in the budget. Funding covers nothing before 1 January 2027. Professional non-profit organisations only; amateur associations and individual artists are directed elsewhere. Material investments, equipment purchases and housing costs are excluded.

item.title: Ernst von Siemens Musikstiftung: Project Funding (October 2026 round)
item.description:
Organisation: Ernst von Siemens Musikstiftung

Location: International, no stated country restriction on the organising institution, though the Foundation is Swiss and German in orientation and administration.

Award: No published minimum or maximum. Primarily covers artistic costs, not overheads. The Foundation explicitly will not fully fund a project, and requires at least one other institution to participate financially at a level similar to the amount requested, functioning as a de facto 1:1 match. No application fee.

Duration: Project-based. The October deadline covers projects beginning the following calendar year.

Deadline: 01 Oct 2026

One of the largest private funders of contemporary and new music in Europe, and it funds the organising side of the field rather than individual artists, which makes it directly usable by festivals. Eligible activity includes festivals, world premieres and revivals, composition commissions, events, academies and workshops, education projects, symposia and musicological publications. Experimental and contemporary sound programming is the core remit; this is not a classical-repertoire fund. There are two annual deadlines: 1 October at 14:00 CEST for projects starting the following year with decisions by year-end, and 1 March for projects starting in July or later with decisions by end of June. Grant sizes are not published, and the Foundation aims funding at artistic rather than overhead costs. Only the organising institution may apply and only legal entities qualify: cultural institutions, orchestra managers, festival organisers and ensembles. Self-applications and applications from individuals are explicitly refused. VOLUME LIMITS are strict and worth planning around: each institution may submit one application per deadline, may be supported for only one project per year, and may be supported for a maximum of three projects across three consecutive years.

item.title: Het Cultuurfonds: Ontwikkelbijdrage for Individual Makers and Collectives (rolling, Netherlands)
item.description:
Organisation: Het Cultuurfonds (formerly Prins Bernhard Cultuurfonds), via voordekunst

Location: Netherlands. Open to individual makers and collectives based in the Netherlands, across all disciplines.

Award: Ontwikkelbijdrage (development contribution) up to EUR 5,000, awarded once every three years. A separate matchfundingbijdrage of EUR 250 to EUR 1,500 (max 50 percent of the crowdfunding target) is available once a year for public-facing projects. No application fee.

Duration: Project or development period; rolling intake with no fixed deadline.

Deadline: Rolling / undated

Since 2025 Het Cultuurfonds runs a dedicated application route for individual makers and collectives, separate from its project grants for foundations and associations. The ontwikkelbijdrage awards up to EUR 5,000 for research, workshops, masterclasses, courses and training, experiments and equipment, and for the pre-phase of a project, giving makers room to test and develop an idea before it has to be fully executed. It is open to all disciplines: visual artists, theatre makers, spoken word artists, photographers, musicians, ceramicists, restorers and more. A separate matchfundingbijdrage of EUR 250 to EUR 1,500 supports crowdfunding campaigns for public-facing projects such as exhibitions or performances. The route is run with voordekunst. Applying is a two-step process: a short vooraanvraag (pre-application) answered within one week, then a full application answered within four weeks, with development funds paid out within two weeks of approval. Rolling intake, no application fee.

item.title: Nordic Culture Point: Culture and Art Programme (autumn 2026 round)
item.description:
Organisation: Nordic Culture Point (Kulturkontakt Nord)

Location: Activity may take place anywhere, but the project must involve partners with addresses in at least three different countries, at least two of which are Nordic (Denmark, Finland, Iceland, Norway, Sweden, Faroe Islands, Greenland, Aland).

Award: Tiered by co-financing: up to EUR 7,000 with NO co-funding required; up to EUR 40,000 with at least 30 percent co-funding; up to EUR 100,000 with at least 50 percent co-funding. In-kind goods and services count toward co-financing. No application fee.

Duration: Project-based. Funded activity may only begin after decision notification, roughly ten weeks after the deadline.

Deadline: 10 Sep 2026

Nordic Culture Point's main project line, funding Nordic collaborative arts and culture projects across all phases: preliminary work, production, presentation and dissemination. Eligible activity explicitly includes creative productions, workshops, knowledge development and spaces for artists to meet publics, which covers festivals, public programmes and convenings when framed as new collaborations. The tiered co-financing model is the standout feature: EUR 7,000 with no match at all, rising to EUR 100,000 at a 50 percent match, and in-kind contributions count. NOTABLE: applicants do not need Nordic residency or citizenship provided the three-country and two-Nordic partner structure is met, so a non-Nordic organisation can lead the project. The autumn window runs 10 August to 10 September 2026, closing 15:59 UTC+3. TIMING RULE: decisions arrive ten weeks after the deadline and no project may start before notification, so budget for a roughly three-month lag. The programme will not finance existing tours, institutional running costs, ongoing festival core financing, solo performances, film, TV or gaming production, or book publishing, so a recurring festival must present a distinct new collaborative strand rather than seek operating support.

item.title: Stimuleringsfonds: Open Call Grounding the Cloud 2026
item.description:
Organisation: Stimuleringsfonds Creatieve Industrie (Creative Industries Fund NL)

Location: Netherlands. Requires Dutch Chamber of Commerce (KvK) registration within the Kingdom of the Netherlands.

Award: Maximum EUR 30,000 per grant. No application fee.

Duration: Project-based; maximum project duration one year.

Deadline: 14 Sep 2026

Open call from the Creative Industries Fund NL (Stimuleringsfonds) for projects within digital culture that provide insight into and reduce the ecological impact of digital technology. Data storage in the cloud, generative AI chatbots and other everyday digital habits carry major ecological consequences: the energy consumption of data centres, the raw materials used for hardware, and ever-growing e-waste. The Fund encourages projects that make the ecological (and therefore also social) impact of digital technologies and data consumption tangible, question it, and put alternative working methods into practice, around topics such as regenerative culture, degrowth, low-tech, the reuse of obsolete hardware, and responsibility for the technologies we use within digital culture. Applications may concern new projects or the reinterpretation or further development of existing initiatives that show scope for more depth or a changed approach. Collaborations in which designers, makers or researchers engage with sustainability from an intersectional perspective are explicitly encouraged. The grant may be used for artistic and substantive development, research, collaboration, knowledge sharing, presentation and documentation. ELIGIBILITY: individual makers, designers, researchers or collectives working on alternative ways of handling digital technology, registered with a Chamber of Commerce within the Kingdom of the Netherlands. Grant awards a maximum of EUR 30,000; maximum project duration one year. This call is open from 17 August 2026, 15:00 CEST until 14 September 2026, 16:00 CEST. No application fee. Questions: digitalecultuur@stimuleringsfonds.nl.

item.title: Nordic Culture Point: Short-term Network Funding, Nordic-Baltic Mobility Programme (autumn 2026)
item.description:
Organisation: Nordic Culture Point (Kulturkontakt Nord)

Location: Nordic and Baltic region. The network must include partners from at least three of: Denmark, Estonia, Finland, Faroe Islands, Greenland, Iceland, Latvia, Lithuania, Norway, Sweden, Aland.

Award: Up to EUR 20,000 for networks lasting one year or less. Nordic Culture Point covers a maximum of 70 percent of the project budget, and combined funding from this programme plus other pan-Nordic bodies may not exceed 85 percent, so at least 15 percent must come from other sources. No application fee.

Duration: Up to one year. Activity may start no earlier than eight weeks after the deadline.

Deadline: 04 Sep 2026

Supports organisations building new cross-border professional networks, funding joint meetings, workshops, staff exchanges and collaborative platforms among artists and cultural practitioners. It is designed for the convening and infrastructure-building side of festival work rather than artistic production, and it explicitly excludes artistic productions and public events, so it is used to assemble festival partners rather than to stage the festival itself. Grants run up to EUR 20,000 for networks of a year or less, with Nordic Culture Point covering at most 70 percent of the budget and a hard 85 percent ceiling on combined pan-Nordic public funding. The autumn 2026 window is 10 August to 4 September 2026, closing 15:59 UTC+3. TIMING RULE: activity may not begin until at least eight weeks after the deadline. IMPORTANT ELIGIBILITY DIFFERENCE from the Culture and Art Programme: the applicant must be resident in a Nordic or Baltic country and must be a professional with documented training or experience in art and culture, so non-Nordic and non-Baltic lead applicants are not eligible. A strong fit for a media-arts or sound-art organisation assembling a regional partner consortium ahead of a larger application.

item.title: NEW FEARS Gallery: Berlin Performance Art Award 2026
item.description:
Organisation: NEW FEARS Gallery

Location: Berlin, Germany (NEW FEARS Gallery, Reichenbergerstrasse 114, 10999 Berlin). Berlin-based applicants only.

Award: Three winning projects each receive a EUR 1,300 grant, shared between the members of a duo or group, plus a ten-day residency at NEW FEARS Gallery, basic technical support and access to the gallery's equipment. The three shortlisted projects that do not win divide 50 percent of the entrance revenue equally. Travel, accommodation, materials, shipping, insurance, per diem and production costs are NOT covered, and artists with a non-German tax number may see tax deducted from the prize at an unstated rate. No application fee.

Duration: Ten-day residency scheduled with the winners during 2026 or 2027; setup the week before 16 October, public performances 16-17 October 2026

Deadline: Closed 15 Aug 2026

NEW FEARS is a Berlin gallery set up as a hybrid space for artists working across choreography and visual art, with a focus on body-based practice, and this award extends that to artists working outside conventional theatre and institutional structures. A jury of Bryana Fritz, Jacopo Lanteri and Burcu Bilgic shortlists six projects, each of which performs live at the gallery on 16 or 17 October 2026; three winners are then chosen and celebrated at Panke Club on 18 October. The application is unusually light: name, email, an optional text of up to 500 words about your work, and up to six links to video documentation with passwords where needed. No CV, no written proposal, no budget, which means the video documentation carries the whole application, so lead with work that shows immediately how it operates live in a gallery. ELIGIBILITY: Berlin-based artists, duos and groups working across performance, choreography, visual art or body-based practice. You must be in Berlin for setup the week before and for the presentations on 16-17 October 2026, and be able to issue an invoice for the award payment. Existing or new work is fine, with no stated duration limits. AVAILABLE EQUIPMENT: sound system, speakers, mixer, LED lights, projector, wind machine, smoke machine, microphone and basic cables; check the venue PDF before proposing anything that depends on a particular room, access route or technical setup. NOTE: the organisers describe this as a DIY, near-zero-budget initiative. There is no production budget and nothing beyond the grant, so a group splitting EUR 1,300 should go in with eyes open. TIMELINE: applications close 15 August 2026 (no time or timezone given); shortlist announced 15 September 2026. Apply through the JotForm at form.jotform.com/261674665583066.

item.title: Berlinale Talents 2027 (Berlin International Film Festival)
item.description:
Organisation: Berlinale / Berlin International Film Festival

Location: Berlin, Germany (during the Berlinale, February 2027); open internationally.

Award: Free participation in the week-long professional program (Summit workshops, Talents Lab, Talent Project Market, industry networking). NO stipend; travel and accommodation are self-covered (national film institutes often fund this; Netherlands-based filmmakers can approach the Netherlands Film Fund). EUR 15 application service fee (EUR 10 early bird before 19 August 2026).

Duration: One week during the Berlinale, February 2027

Deadline: 02 Sep 2026

item.title: Privacy Camp 2026 (EDRi): Call for Sessions, The Origins of Future Technologies
item.description:
Organisation: European Digital Rights (EDRi), with LSTS at Vrije Universiteit Brussel, Privacy Salon vzw, the Institute for European Studies at Université Saint-Louis Bruxelles, and the Racism and Technology Center

Location: Brussels, Belgium, and online (hybrid). Event on 13 October 2026.

Award: NO speaker fee or honorarium. Where needed, up to EUR 400 per speaker or session organiser towards transport to and accommodation in Brussels, reimbursed against invoices and travel tickets; those with organisational support are encouraged to cover their own expenses. No budget beyond this cap. Free to propose and free to attend (registration open).

Duration: One-day conference on 13 October 2026. Average session length 50 minutes.

Deadline: Closed 10 Aug 2026

Privacy Camp holds its 14th edition on 13 October 2026 in Brussels and online, organised by European Digital Rights (EDRi) with the Research Group on Law, Science, Technology & Society (LSTS) at Vrije Universiteit Brussel, Privacy Salon vzw, the Institute for European Studies at Université Saint-Louis Bruxelles, and the Racism and Technology Center. THEME: 'The Origins of Future Technologies: Towards communities of digital self-determination'. The call starts from the premise that digital futures do not appear from nowhere but are built through land, labour, capital, infrastructure, law, public money, political choices and social struggle, and asks where technologies come from, who gets to shape them, and what conditions make digital self-determination possible. It situates this against the EU's 2026 Tech Sovereignty Package (semiconductors, artificial intelligence, cloud infrastructure and data centres) and the wider deregulatory agenda including the Digital Omnibus, the AI Omnibus and reforms affecting data protection, privacy, labour and environmental safeguards, asking whose version of sovereignty is actually being discussed. TOPIC AREAS: (1) Material conditions in the production of technologies, covering the natural resources needed across the supply chain (critical components such as semiconductors, water for data centres) and how GDPR, ePrivacy and AI Act safeguards shape the material conditions of AI from data extraction and biometric processing through to data centres, labour and public infrastructure; labour conditions, including who mines critical materials, union-busting across the tech supply chain, and coalitions between tech workers, unions, migrant justice groups, climate movements and digital rights organisations; and capital, meaning the venture capital forces driving the current AI hype and consolidating through defence, security and militarisation. (2) Political vision in the use of technologies, covering military use and how militarisation and securitisation shape the EU deregulation debate, and the political ideologies driving technology development, including what digital self-determination means for communities facing racialised discrimination, surveillance, occupation, border violence, workplace control or environmental harm. (3) Moving technologies forward through communities, covering community innovation for digital self-determination (distributed and self-hosted data storage, AI built by and for community needs, community-led, public or cooperative digital infrastructure); law, deregulation and rights (resisting the Digital Omnibus and specifically the Data Omnibus, defending GDPR and ePrivacy safeguards, protecting access, transparency and automated decision-making rights, enforcing existing digital laws, supporting collective litigation, and challenging the framing of rights as obstacles to EU competitiveness); and building power by connecting grassroots movements across tech worker organising, labour, migrant, LGBTQIA+, climate, economic justice and landback movements. FORMATS: interactive workshops are particularly encouraged, meaning small-group work, peer exchange and collaboration across sectors, coalitions and disciplines, moving from talk to strategic action; panel discussions are also welcome, especially those centring diverse voices and grounded lived experience with room for meaningful audience engagement. SUBMISSION GUIDELINES: state a clear objective for the session and what a good outcome would be; make it as interactive as possible; support a diversity of voices and multiple perspectives; average session length is 50 minutes; propose the format that actually suits the idea rather than forcing a panel into a workshop or vice versa. For workshops, make the objectives, structure and facilitation clear and have participants work together in small groups towards a specific goal; the organisers provide additional guidance, support and feedback for workshops. For panels, list a maximum of 4 speakers covering academia, civil society and decision-maker perspectives, and indicate which speakers have confirmed at least in principle. TIMELINE: proposals due via the online form by 10 August 2026 at 09:00 CEST; the Content Committee notifies applicants before 21 August 2026; confirmation to proceed required by 25 August; draft programme published 4 September; speakers and final session description confirmed by 10 September at the latest (earlier confirmation improves the odds that the EUR 400 reimbursement budget covers speaker travel and accommodation); final programme published 28 September. The 2026 Content Committee is Andreea Belu (EDRi), Gloria González Fuster (LSTS, VUB), Jill Toh (Racism and Technology Center), Sanne Stevens (Justice, Equity and Technology Project) and Alexandra Giannopoulou (DFF). Programme enquiries: andreea.belu@edri.org. Venue and reimbursement enquiries: guillermo.peris@edri.org.

Location: European Union, United Kingdom, Armenia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Kosovo, Montenegro, North Macedonia and Serbia. All coalition partners must be based and operating in these countries.

Deadline: Closed 07 Aug 2026

NOTE: this is a gender-equality movement-building fund rather than an arts or technology programme, and it is coalition-only (no individual applicants). Relevance to creative or tech practice runs through the narrative-change and digital-storytelling strand of the call. The Alliance for Gender Equality in Europe, a philanthropic initiative created in 2021 and hosted by the Network of European Foundations, is launching an open call under its forthcoming Strengthening Movements Fund. The Alliance is composed of the Bodossaki Foundation, Fondation BNP Paribas, Fondation CHANEL, Fondazione con il Sud, Fondation de France, Fondation RAJA-Danièle Marcovici, King Baudouin Foundation and L'Oréal Fund for Women; this particular fund is backed by all of those except Fondation BNP Paribas. OBJECTIVE: to foster collaboration and solidarity within European intersectional and grassroots movements so that they can collectively advance gender equality in Europe in the long term. The call follows a 2025 Alliance-commissioned mapping of European gender-equality movements (30 in-depth interviews plus contextual research) which found movements under-resourced because philanthropic funding frameworks are misaligned with their needs; the fund is designed to replace short-term reactive funding with proactive long-term support. OUTCOMES SOUGHT: community organising reinforced at local or national level; pan-European feminist collaborations and solidarity strengthened; alliances between gender equality and other social justice movements expanded; pro-gender-equality narratives and voices amplified in local, national, regional or digital spaces; policy debates informed by feminist and gender equality movements. ELIGIBLE ACTIVITIES INCLUDE (non-exhaustive): national, regional or pan-European convenings and collaborative projects where groups co-create joint strategies; joint campaigns between feminist movements and allied movements (climate justice, anti-racism, LGBTQI+, disability rights); narrative-change training for grassroots groups covering framing, messaging, digital tools and digital storytelling; cross-border coalitions advocating EU institutions or national governments; facilitated virtual or in-person convenings to work through internal tensions and build trust; translating academic research on anti-gender efforts into movement strategies. ELIGIBILITY: collective proposals with at least 3 organisations per coalition (no maximum); legally registered non-profits (NGOs, civil society organisations, social enterprises, national or regional funds); based and operating in the target countries; small and medium grassroots organisations, defined by annual budget under EUR 450,000 (Austria, Belgium, Denmark, Finland, France, Germany, Ireland, Luxembourg, Netherlands, Sweden, UK) or under EUR 300,000 (Armenia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Bulgaria, Croatia, Republic of Cyprus, Czechia, Estonia, Greece, Hungary, Italy, Kosovo, Latvia, Lithuania, Malta, Montenegro, North Macedonia, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain, Serbia). Intermediary organisations and networks are exempt from the budget thresholds but must apply in coalition with grassroots organisations, with the budget fairly distributed among all partners. Coalitions must be community-led (majority of leadership roles held by members of the community supported, and/or participatory approaches), work with marginalised women, transgender, non-binary and gender non-conforming people, use gender transformative approaches, and hold an intersectional perspective. Proposals must be completed in English. Each organisation may submit only one application, as lead or as partner. One organisation per coalition acts as lead, is the primary contact and is legally responsible for the grant; leads are invited to networking, peer-learning and capacity-strengthening activities. SCORING (100 points): relevance to the call objective 20; demonstrated track record in strengthening movements 20 (learnings valued as well as achievements); strong impact 25 (must contribute to at least one of the five outcomes, with clear measurement); ability to work collaboratively and inclusively with partners 20 (including fair budget repartition); quality and feasibility 15. item.title: Open Call: Pee Workshop (Matter Out of Place)
item.description:
Organisation: Nica Roses & Eris Kyriakides, at The Dirty Art Foundation

Location: The Dirty Art Foundation (Amsterdam, Netherlands)

Award: Performer fee of EUR 200. Participation in the optional public showing is not required to receive the fee.

Duration: Two-day workshop, Monday 17 and Tuesday 18 August 2026, 10:00-17:00, with an optional 60-minute public showing on Wednesday 19 August

Deadline: Closed 10 Aug 2026

Pee Workshop is looking for 16 performers to take part in a two-day research practice led by Nica Roses and Eris Kyriakides as part of the dance and performance event Matter Out of Place. The workshop uses drinking, holding, and releasing liquid as a starting point for choreographic research, paying attention to the body's internal timing: what we consume, how liquid moves through the body, what the bladder signals, and how the organs produce movements that often go unnoticed. This cycle becomes the structure of the research, opening into dance, somatic exercises, choreographic tasks, group compositions, and experiments with collective energy. The material develops through urination but also through the shared experience of moving, waiting, responding, and performing together. Performers, dancers, movement practitioners, and artists interested in somatic research, experimental choreography, and collective performance-making are welcome; professional dance training is not required, but applicants should feel comfortable working physically and collaboratively. All exercises are approached through clear consent, respect for personal boundaries, and collective care. The workshop takes place Monday 17 and Tuesday 18 August 2026 from 10:00 to 17:00 at The Dirty Art Foundation, culminating in an optional 60-minute public showing on Wednesday 19 August. Each performer receives a fee of EUR 200. To apply, send a short introduction about yourself, your movement or performance experience, and why you are interested in the workshop to nicaxroses@gmail.com by 10 August 2026.
